01_static_server: With `-p`, a relative `root` is resolved against the exercise directory, and `index` must name a file that exists there.
02_config_layout: `nginx -T` prints every file that was actually loaded; if your server block is missing from it, the `include` line is not active.
03_context_hierarchy: Read the first `[emerg]` line from `nginx -t` and ask which enclosing block that directive belongs in: `http`, `server`, or `location`.
04_worker_user: `user` must name the account that runs Nginxlings (see `id -un`), and `root` must point at this exercise's own `html/` directory instead of a distro path.
05_install_verify: The image starts without NGINX: install the distribution package in a `RUN` step so that `nginx -v` works inside the container.
06_reverse_proxy: The empty `location /` serves local files; give it a directive that forwards the request to the backend on 127.0.0.1:8080.
07_http_load_balancer: Define an `upstream` that lists both backends and send `location /` to it; the `upstream=` field in the container logs shows who answered each request.
08_stream_load_balancer: Layer 4 has no `location` blocks: define a top-level `stream {}` next to `http`, not inside it, and hand the whole `server` to the upstream by name.
09_shared_zones_basics: A zone is declared once in `http` with a name and a size, and does nothing until a `limit_req` in a `server` or `location` refers to it by name.
10_upstream_status_zone: Give the upstream a `zone`, then add `resolve` to each server so the Docker DNS names are looked up at runtime instead of at startup.
11_zone_sync_api: An exact-match `location =` can serve the bundled JSON file; without a MIME map you must set the Content-Type yourself with `default_type`.
12_logs_and_variables: Define `log_format main` once in `http`, then point `access_log` at `/dev/stdout` with that format name.
13_include_modular_config: `include` pastes the file in place, so put each `include` inside the block whose directives that file contains.
14_multi_domain_static: Send the same request with different `Host` headers: each `server_name` should land in its own `server` block with its own `root`.
15_https_tls: Both listeners need a `server` block; only the HTTPS one uses `ssl` on its `listen` line and points at the certificate and key already built into the image.
16_shared_zone_sizing: The NGINX docs say a 1 MB zone keeps about 16 thousand 64-byte states; estimate how many distinct keys the check creates and size the zone to hold them.
17_verify_nginx_user: Without a `user` directive the workers run as a default account; run `ps aux` inside the container to see which one, then set the account you want.
18_osi_layers_usecases: `stream` sits beside `http` at the top level, and its dynamic module must be loaded with `load_module` at the very top of nginx.conf.
